164889003.text: An ECG showing atrial fibrillation. Irregularly irregular RR intervals with no distinct P waves; the baseline shows fibrillatory f waves and the ventricular rhythm varies beat to beat.

164890007.text: An ECG showing atrial flutter. Regular atrial activity at about 250 to 350 per minute producing sawtooth flutter waves, best seen in leads II, III, aVF and V1, often with fixed 2:1 or variable atrioventricular conduction.

6374002.text: An ECG showing bundle branch block. Delayed ventricular conduction through one bundle branch giving a widened QRS complex of 120 ms or more with abnormal terminal QRS morphology.

426627000.text: An ECG showing bradycardia. Ventricular rate below 60 beats per minute regardless of the underlying rhythm.

164909002.text: An ECG showing left bundle branch block. QRS duration of 120 ms or more with broad notched R waves in I, aVL, V5 and V6, absent septal q waves in lateral leads and deep S waves in V1, with discordant ST-T changes.

59118001.text: An ECG showing right bundle branch block. QRS duration of 120 ms or more with an rsR' pattern in V1 and V2 and a wide slurred S wave in leads I and V6.

270492004.text: An ECG showing first degree atrioventricular block. Every P wave is conducted to the ventricles but the PR interval is prolonged beyond 200 ms.

713426002.text: An ECG showing incomplete right bundle branch block. rsR' pattern in V1 and V2 resembling right bundle branch block but with QRS duration between 110 and 120 ms.

39732003.text: An ECG showing left axis deviation. Mean frontal plane QRS axis more negative than minus 30 degrees: positive QRS in lead I and predominantly negative QRS in leads II and aVF.

445118002.text: An ECG showing left anterior fascicular block. Left axis deviation between minus 45 and minus 90 degrees with qR in I and aVL, rS in II, III and aVF, and QRS duration under 120 ms.

251146004.text: An ECG showing low QRS voltages. Small QRS amplitudes: peak-to-peak below 0.5 mV in all limb leads or below 1.0 mV in all precordial leads.

698252002.text: An ECG showing nonspecific intraventricular conduction disturbance. QRS duration above 110 ms without the morphology criteria of left or right bundle branch block.

426783006.text: An ECG showing sinus rhythm. Normal sinus rhythm: upright P wave in leads I and II before every QRS complex, constant PR interval and a regular rate between 60 and 100 beats per minute.

63593006.text: An ECG showing supraventricular premature beats. Premature atrial or junctional beats: early narrow QRS complexes preceded by an abnormal or hidden P wave, usually followed by a non-compensatory pause.

10370003.text: An ECG showing pacing rhythm. Electronic pacemaker rhythm with sharp pacing spikes preceding paced P waves or wide paced QRS complexes.

17338001.text: An ECG showing ventricular premature beats. Premature wide and bizarre QRS complexes not preceded by a P wave, with discordant T waves and usually a full compensatory pause.

164947007.text: An ECG showing prolonged PR interval. PR interval longer than 200 ms, measured from the onset of the P wave to the onset of the QRS complex.

111975006.text: An ECG showing prolonged QT interval. Heart-rate corrected QT interval prolonged, above about 450 ms in men or 460 ms in women, reflecting delayed ventricular repolarization.

164917005.text: An ECG showing Q wave abnormal. Pathological Q waves wider than 40 ms or deeper than one quarter of the following R wave, suggesting prior myocardial necrosis.

47665007.text: An ECG showing right axis deviation. Mean frontal plane QRS axis greater than plus 90 degrees: negative QRS in lead I and positive QRS in lead aVF.

427393009.text: An ECG showing sinus arrhythmia. Sinus P waves with normal morphology but phasic variation of the PP interval by more than 0.12 seconds, typically with respiration.

426177001.text: An ECG showing sinus bradycardia. Sinus rhythm with normal P waves before each QRS complex at a rate below 60 beats per minute.

427084000.text: An ECG showing sinus tachycardia. Sinus rhythm with normal P waves before each QRS complex at a rate above 100 beats per minute.

164934002.text: An ECG showing T wave abnormal. Abnormal T waves that are flattened, low amplitude, biphasic or inverted in leads where they are normally upright, indicating abnormal repolarization.

59931005.text: An ECG showing T wave inversion. Negative T waves in leads where the T wave is normally positive, such as I, II and V3 to V6.

164865005.text: An ECG showing myocardial infarction. Evidence of myocardial infarction: pathological Q waves, loss of R wave amplitude and ST-T changes in contiguous leads matching a coronary territory.

164873001.text: An ECG showing left ventricular hypertrophy. Increased QRS voltage over the left ventricle, for example S in V1 plus R in V5 or V6 above 35 mm, often with lateral ST depression and T inversion of strain pattern.

429622005.text: An ECG showing ST depression. Horizontal or downsloping depression of the ST segment of at least 0.5 mm below the PR baseline in two contiguous leads.

164931005.text: An ECG showing ST elevation. Elevation of the ST segment at the J point above the baseline in two or more contiguous leads.

55827005.text: An ECG showing left ventricular high voltage. Increased QRS amplitudes in left precordial or limb leads meeting voltage criteria without other features of hypertrophy.

195042002.text: An ECG showing second degree atrioventricular block. Intermittent failure of atrioventricular conduction: some P waves are not followed by a QRS complex, with or without progressive PR prolongation.

233917008.text: An ECG showing atrioventricular block. Impaired conduction from atria to ventricles shown by prolonged PR interval or P waves not followed by QRS complexes.

428750005.text: An ECG showing nonspecific ST-T abnormality. Minor ST segment deviation or T wave flattening that does not meet criteria for ischemia, injury or a specific diagnosis.

67741000119109.text: An ECG showing left atrial enlargement. Broad notched P wave longer than 120 ms in lead II with a deep terminal negative P component in V1.

446358003.text: An ECG showing right atrial hypertrophy. Tall peaked P waves above 2.5 mm in the inferior leads indicating right atrial enlargement.

89792004.text: An ECG showing right ventricular hypertrophy. Right axis deviation with dominant R wave in V1 and deep S waves in V5 and V6 indicating right ventricular hypertrophy.

713422000.text: An ECG showing atrial tachycardia. Regular narrow complex tachycardia above 100 per minute with non-sinus P waves of uniform abnormal morphology.

426761007.text: An ECG showing supraventricular tachycardia. Rapid regular narrow QRS tachycardia above 150 beats per minute originating above the ventricles, with P waves hidden or retrograde.

251198002.text: An ECG showing clockwise cardiac rotation. Delayed precordial transition with the R/S ratio becoming greater than one only in V5 or V6.

251199005.text: An ECG showing counterclockwise cardiac rotation. Early precordial transition with dominant R waves already in V1 or V2.

164912004.text: An ECG showing P wave change. Abnormal P wave morphology, amplitude or axis compared with normal sinus P waves.

164930006.text: An ECG showing ST interval abnormal. Abnormal ST segment shape or level not meeting specific elevation or depression criteria.

164937009.text: An ECG showing U wave abnormal. Prominent or inverted U waves following the T wave.

input_spec.source: our 100 Hz 0.5-45 Hz band-passed mV, upsampled x5 (resample_poly)

notes.method: MERL zero-shot (Liu et al., ICML 2024, arXiv 2403.06659), official code and released checkpoint, no training or fine-tuning on any of our data.
notes.pretraining_data: MIMIC-IV-ECG v1.0 (BIDMC, Boston; 771,693 ECG-report pairs, 500 Hz, 10 s). It shares no records with our databases (CPSC2018/CPSC-Extra, PTB-XL, Georgia, Shaoxing/Ningbo), which come from other hospitals and countries.
notes.checkpoint_selection_caveat: The released *_best_ckpt.pth was selected during pretraining by the average zero-shot AUROC on the validation splits of PTB-XL (super/sub/form/rhythm), CPSC2018 (ICBEB) and Chapman-Shaoxing (CSN) (see utils/utils_trainer.py and pretrain/config.yaml val_sets). Those are part of our CPSC, PTBXL and SHAONING test sets. MERL never trained on them, but it was model-selected on them, and its CKEPE prompts were written for their class names. GEORGIA was never used.
notes.paper_eval: The paper evaluates zero-shot on PTB-XL (4 subsets), CPSC2018 and CSN test splits, with dataset-specific label sets. Our evaluation uses our SNOMED vocabulary and protocol, so the numbers are not comparable to the paper's.
